trace_interpretation: For a ~1.49 MB multipart POST, libcurl normally adds Expect: 100-continue. The client received only 100 and then broken pipe, which is consistent with the handshake being involved but does not prove it caused the interruption. Earlier successful WLED uploads used the same multipart route; their response receipts do not preserve request headers.

materially_corrected_method.preserve: exact same multipart field, artifact bytes, WLED 16.0.1 /update target, local source, timeouts; one request only
materially_corrected_method.change: add curl header override -H 'Expect:' to suppress Expect: 100-continue; no HTTP version, endpoint, artifact, or payload change
materially_corrected_method.why: addresses the only newly visible transfer behavior in the failed trace and keeps the known-good WLED multipart consumer contract. Not represented as proven root cause.

primary_sources.title: curl FAQ: My HTTP POST or PUT requests are slow
primary_sources.material_fact: libcurl normally uses Expect: 100-continue for larger POST/PUT bodies and says it can be disabled by overriding the header with -H / CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER.
